note: The MCP arm has 88 GitHub tools; the mirage arm has `/template` for reads and `gh` for everything else, with `gh api` as the general form. These cases pair the operations this task's agent actually performs.

cases.name: file_contents
cases.why: the same file reads back byte for byte through either arm
cases.note: `get_file_contents` decodes; the contents endpoint returns base64, so the mirage side decodes with jq's @base64d

cases.name: list_branches
cases.why: both arms see the same branches

cases.name: list_commits
cases.why: the same history, in the same order

cases.name: owner_repos
cases.why: both arms enumerate the same repositories for the account, and they reach it two different ways: `search_repositories` goes through `/search/repositories` with a `user:` qualifier where `gh api users/<owner>/repos` is scoped by its path. This case was a declared divergence until strukto-ai/mirage#981 -- the fake dropped every qualifier, so `user:integ-user` and `user:Toolathlon-Archive` both answered with all ten repositories. It was the only divergence where the two arms saw different worlds, and it is kept as a case because one arm's route is still the only thing that reaches that endpoint

cases.name: emails_get_folders
cases.why: both arms list the same IMAP folders

cases.name: emails_get_emails
cases.why: the same messages, in the same order, through either arm

cases.name: emails_search_emails
cases.why: a search returns the same hits

cases.name: create_file
cases.why: a commit through either arm leaves the same tree behind

mirage.command: gh api repos/integ-user/My-Homepage/contents/parity.md -X PUT -f message='parity check' -f branch=master -f content=cGFyaXR5Cg==

cases.name: create_repo_refused
cases.why: this task's token cannot create a repository from nothing on either arm, so neither arm has a path the other lacks
cases.note: the arms word the refusal differently -- the MCP server returns its wrapper's message, mirage surfaces the fake's 403 -- so the projection asserts the fact rather than the wording, and fails the case if a repository comes back. Nothing here is solved by creating one (all five repositories are seeded before the first turn, and a fresh one has no history in common with the archive, so the grader's compare 404s), which is why this case guards a constraint rather than closing an exploit
